speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in view of rising global food prices and export controls imposed on rice and its substitutes, what measures will the Ministry implement to mitigate the impact and assist the lower- and middle-income groups.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the upcoming inflationary outlook in view of the latest rising food and energy prices; and (b) what are the further measures to mitigate the impact to households and businesses.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Inflation in Singapore has eased in recent months.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Similarly, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) Core Inflation eased from 5.5% to 3.8% over the same period.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For the rest of 2023, inflation should slow further as import costs are likely to remain lower relative to a year ago.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Nevertheless, upside risks remain, including from further shocks to the global economy and global commodity prices and supply chains.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government has taken a multi-pronged approach to help households and businesses cope with inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have introduced measures to help lower- and middle-income households manage the higher cost of living.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government is also helping businesses manage rising costs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For instance, we enhanced the Enterprise Financing Scheme in Budget 2023 to reduce businesses’ borrowing needs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To mitigate higher energy prices, Government schemes, such as the Energy Efficiency Grant and the Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions, help businesses become more energy-efficient.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will continue to keep the Singapore dollar strong, which dampens imported inflation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Price Kaki, of course, promotes price transparency by providing easy and timely comparisons of grocery and hawker food prices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will continue to monitor trends in inflation and do even more to help Singaporeans, businesses and households, if necessary.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider efforts to encourage our consumers to switch to non-basmati white rice alternatives, some of which may even be healthier or more nutritious, in order to diversify away from our country's reliance on white rice imports?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Maybe also to share a little bit of background on global rice prices.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But if you look at the global rice of most other food commodities, they have fallen.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The overall FAO Food Price Index has actually dropped by 11.8% in August year-on-year.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I am giving Members the bigger picture so that we can see how we can better address this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government has also then strengthened food supply resilience both by diversifying the food import sources as well as encouraging local production.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, in July 2023, when India banned the non-basmati white rice exports, we requested the Indian government for waiver from the ban for our domestic food security requirements.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Indian government acceded, and our multiple import sources and our rice stockpile scheme have also allowed us to mitigate the impact of these disruptions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also encourage Singaporeans to widen their choice of food, including different kinds of rice.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also encourage everyone to use the Price Kaki app by CASE to choose as well as to find out the prices of rice between different retailers as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are different sources of rice and different prices of rice as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The other question is on the trend of the energy and commodity prices.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: They are all elevated back again, and I wanted to know what MTI can do to help moderate some of these cost pressures, especially to the businesses.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the impact, particularly on the lower- and middle-income households, in fact, if you look at the January to June figures, the impact of inflation rates were lower for low-income households.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it is less for the lower-income group.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Also, as Minister of State Chee mentioned earlier, the Government will look at ways to further help Singaporeans, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: All in all, what the Government is doing is also on the fiscal stance but on the monetary policy stance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And it is for MAS to continue the current stance of appreciating the Singapore dollar to dampen imported inflation.
